source_provenance_limit: Existing local fixed Java snapshot receipt reused; no fresh tree/blob/archive binding. NeoForge/data-component API is adjacent reference, not Dynasty native target.
findings: Legacy deserializeNBT explicitly normalizes Compartments wrong cardinality to8 EMPTY before parent inventory load. This remains the narrow accepted behavior.

Modern CODEC uses ItemSlots.maxSizeCodec(32) for item map but OPTIONAL_CODEC.listOf for filters with no visible eight-entry validator. STREAM_CODEC uses unrestricted ItemSlots stream codec plus filter list; neither calls legacy deserializeNBT.

Private deserialize creates32-slot null-owner inventory, settling=true while setStackInSlot still accesses filters, then replaces filters with decoded list without cardinality normalization. settling avoids settle callbacks, not setStackInSlot filter access.

Component registration uses backwards-compatible persistent codec and stream codec; fallback ItemContainerContents constructs default8filters and fillshandler, distinct from modern record branch. Do not generalize legacy cardinality protection to every input path.

applyImplicitComponents reads TOOLBOX_INVENTORY through readInventory. readInventory copies inv.filters first then sets each item; empty/short filters plus nonempty slot can reach filters.get(slot/4). isItemValid and tickPlayers also index filters.

Persistent ItemSlots maxSize validates total size<=32 after highest-slot consistency; stream codec has no visible nonnegative/max-size validation. Unknown native codecs may validate individual item values; not an end-to-end runtime crash assertion.
application_to_dynasty: Apply the same owner schema invariants to each persistent/network/component ingress. Existing legacy validation alone does not establish all migration paths protected; native target/parser behavior must be verified before any repair.
